Their head coach was [[Matt Painter]], who is in his 21st season with the Boilermakers. The Boilermakers played their home games at [[Mackey Arena]] in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Boilermakers were ranked No. 1 in the preseason [[AP poll|AP]] and coaches polls, the first time the school had begun the season ranked in the top spot.{{Cite web |last=read |first=Ryan YoungStaff writer·5 min |date=2025-10-13 |title=Men's basketball AP preseason poll: Purdue takes No. 1 spot as Houston, Florida trail close behind |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mens-college-basketball/breaking-news/article/mens-basketball-ap-preseason-poll-purdue-takes-no-1-spot-as-houston-florida-trail-close-behind-161143102.html |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} Prior to the regular season, they won the [[Bahamas Championship]], defeating [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.journalgazette.net/sports/colleges/purdue/purdue-basketball-season-in-review-how-good-is-good-enough/article_5ff7210d-6651-4699-8b4a-ce9b09eaf5b9.html|title=Purdue Basketball Season in Review: How good is good enough?|publisher=The Journal Gazette|date=30 March 2026|accessdate=11 May 2026}} The Boilermakers finished the regular season 23–8 (13–7 in the [[2025-26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten]]).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/schedule/_/id/2509/purdue-boilermakers|title=Purdue Boilermakers Schedule 2025-26|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=11 May 2026}} They then won the [[2026 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten Championship]], defeating [[2025-26 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/59631/|title=Purdue Wins the 2026 TIAA Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament Championship|author=Big Ten Communications|publisher=Big Ten|date=15 March 2026|accessdate=11 May 2026}} As champions, they received an automatic bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the West region. There they defeated [[2025-26 Queens Royals men's basketball team|Queens]] in the first round{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2026/03/20/purdue-basketball-queens-score-march-madness-ncaa-tournament/89190042007/|title=Braden Smith, Purdue basketball power past Queens in March Madness|author=Sam King|publisher=Lafayette Journal and Courier|date=20 March 2026|accessdate=11 May 2026}} and [[2025-26 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] in the second round to make the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Sweet 16]] for the third year in a row.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2026/03/22/purdue-basketball-miami-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-score/89260258007/|title=Senior duo powers Purdue to March
